items.title: Press Briefing Note by Hon. Minister for Foreign Affairs on Bhote Koshi Flood
items.summary: The Government of Nepal has mobilized search, rescue, relief and recovery operations across Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading and Chitwan districts following the 26 August 2026 Bhote Koshi floods, with an Emergency Control Room established at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs to coordinate with families of missing foreign nationals. So far 626 bodies have been recovered and over 4450 people rescued, including over 187 foreign nationals, while about 2400 people remain unaccounted for. Specialized assistance has been requested from neighbors, with an Indian tunnel rescue team already mobilized and a Chinese team expected, alongside relief materials received from India, China, Japan and Australia.
items.citation: Nepal Ministry of Foreign Affairs — Press Briefing Note by Hon. Minister for Foreign Affairs on Bhote Koshi Flood

items.title: Latest Updates on Flash Floods- 28 August 2026
items.summary: Severe flash floods struck the Bhote Koshi River area of Nepal on 26 August 2026, causing loss of life, displacement, and damage to infrastructure. So far, 538 bodies have been recovered from the river areas. Out of 632 people from 33 countries, 121 have been found and 511 are still missing, with search and rescue operations continuing.
items.citation: Nepal Ministry of Foreign Affairs — Latest Updates on Flash Floods- 28 August 2026

items.title: FOCUS | Rescue operations at mudslide-hit border port in SW China's Xizang
items.summary: Rescue operations intensified at the mudslide-stricken Gyirong Port in Xizang on Thursday, with 141 rescuers arriving that morning and another 111 from the China Search and Rescue team reaching Gyirong County by afternoon. As of 8 a.m. Thursday, three people had been killed, 558 others remained missing, and two local villagers had been rescued after the mudslide struck the port on Wednesday morning. The Red Cross Society of China dispatched a team and allocated 2,500 sets of supplies including tents, quilts, and hygiene kits, while the Chinese Red Cross Foundation provided more than 5,500 boxes of food and water.
items.citation: Xinhua (Gyirong / Tibet side) — FOCUS | Rescue operations at mudslide-hit border port in SW China's Xizang

items.title: Latest Updates on Flash Floods-27 August 2026
items.summary: Flash floods struck the Bhote Koshi River area of Nepal on 26 August 2026, causing loss of life, displacement, and damage to houses, roads, bridges, and other infrastructure. As of 20:00 hrs NST on 27 August 2026, 359 bodies have been recovered while 596 people from 33 countries remain missing. Security agencies and local authorities are conducting ongoing search, rescue, and relief operations.

items.title: NOTICE: Emergency Control Room (ECR) for Assistance regarding Foreign Nationals Affected by the Bhote Koshi Flash Flood
items.summary: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs has established an Emergency Control Room to coordinate search, rescue, information verification, and consular assistance for foreign nationals affected by or missing in the Rasuwa flash flood. Families and diplomatic missions may contact the ECR via hotline or WhatsApp at +977-9744441227 or +977-9744441228 (7am–10pm) or through official channels for updates on affected foreign nationals. The Ministry requests that all parties rely solely on verified official sources and will post further information at https://mofa.gov.np/category/flashflood/.
items.citation: Nepal Ministry of Foreign Affairs — NOTICE: Emergency Control Room (ECR) for Assistance regarding Foreign Nationals Affected by the Bhote Koshi Flash Flood

items.title: Special Control Room in MEA for Nepal Floods Situation
items.summary: The Ministry of External Affairs has established a 24×7 Special Control Room in Delhi for the Nepal floods situation. Contact options include the control room numbers +91 11 2308 8718, +91 11 2308 8719 and +91 11 2301 2113, WhatsApp +91 9968291988, and email situationroom@mea.gov.in. Indian embassies in Kathmandu and Beijing provide additional WhatsApp contacts, while Nepali authorities listed include the Tourist Police, Nepal Army, NDRRMA, and district officers for Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading and Chitwan.
items.citation: MEA press release — Special Control Room in MEA for Nepal Floods Situation

items.title: Latest Updates on Flash Floods- 26 August 2026
items.summary: Flash floods struck the Bhote Koshi River on 26 August 2026, causing loss of life, displacement, and damage to homes, roads, bridges, and hydropower facilities. So far, 72 bodies have been recovered while 403 people from 25 countries (203 males and 200 females, including 62 Nepali nationals) are reported missing. Security agencies and authorities are conducting search and rescue, evacuation, and relief operations.
items.citation: Nepal Ministry of Foreign Affairs — Latest Updates on Flash Floods- 26 August 2026

items.title: NDRRMA rescue coordination portal
items.summary: NDRRMA publishes rescue and coordination updates for the Bhotekoshi/Rasuwa flash flood on its official rescue portal and the SETU platform at setu.ndrrma.gov.np. Families should use these official channels for status rather than unofficial social media reposts. This site links to NDRRMA and does not copy individual case data.

items.title: Nepal Police official found and missing lists
items.summary: Nepal Police maintains the official Unified Database for missing persons, found persons, and unidentified remains related to the flood-affected areas. Families can search the database at udb.nepalpolice.gov.np/missing and udb.nepalpolice.gov.np/found. Official confirmation of status comes only from Nepal Police and not from volunteer sites or social media.

items.title: Embassy of India, Kathmandu — assistance for Indian nationals
items.summary: The Embassy of India in Kathmandu is coordinating with Nepalese authorities on search and rescue for Indian nationals affected by flash floods in the Rasuwa/Bhotekoshi area. Indian nationals and families may contact the MEA Special Control Room in Delhi at +91-11-23088718, +91-11-23088719, WhatsApp +91-9968291988, or email situationroom@mea.gov.in. The Embassy may also be reached via WhatsApp at +977-9851316807.
